subject: CloudBridge partner paper: reseller pass-through & evidence scope
messages:
From: Rebecca Li <rebecca@cloudbridge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudBridge Legal <legal@cloudbridge.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Partner paper redlines — pass-through and audit evidence

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week — CloudBridge is excited to move forward. Our legal team attached redlines to your partner paper focused on how marketplace fees are treated when CloudBridge resells Redwood capacity through the marketplace. The key items we highlighted:

- A pass-through clause that allows CloudBridge to invoice our customers for platform fees (marketplace cut).
- Audit/evidence scope: we propose limited audit rights tied to invoicing and payment reconciliation (not broad access to logs).
- Order Form language that maps fees to the billing waterfall so customers know which entity invoices which portion.

Please review the attached redlines and confirm whether Redwood requires any additional evidence we must provide for accounting/ops reconciliation. We flagged items where we think a short, mutual definition of "pass-through charges" would help.

Attachments: CloudBridge-pass-through-redlines.docx

Would prefer a short sync early next week to close these, and ideally a one-page MAP for procurement + finance.

Thanks,
Rebecca Li
Head of Strategic Partnerships
CloudBridge

---
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-30T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Partner paper redlines — pass-through and audit evidence

Rebecca — thanks for sending these over and for the clear callouts. Looping in Ben (sales) and Laura (legal ops) to scope the review.

Quick notes from our side:
- We are open to a defined pass-through for marketplace fees, but need to narrow the permitted charges to (a) platform/marketplace fees actually charged by the reseller channel and (b) transaction passthroughs (no markup category).
- For audit/evidence, Redwood can accept a staged evidence handoff: payment reconciliation reports + invoice copies + attestation from the marketplace. We want to avoid granting broad log-level access unless there is a narrow, contractually-triggered audit.
- Order Form: we prefer a short waterfall table that sits in the Order Form (or an exhibit) referencing which party issues invoice lines. That keeps the MSA clean and keeps commercial flow explicit.

I've attached an internal checklist (pass-through-evidence-checklist.xlsx) to get the ops questions surfaced — please take a look and comment on what CloudBridge can produce by contract signature vs. upon audit request. Also attaching an initial MSA redline we may propose back (redlines_msa_v1.docx).

Proposed next steps:
1) CloudBridge to confirm the limited list of pass-through charges (reply in-line on the checklist).
2) Redwood legal to produce clean language for the MSA + Order Form waterfall (Laura, can you take point?).
3) Joint MAP for procurement and finance with timelines (Ben to lead commercial).

Can we tentatively book a 30-minute sync on Monday 12/6? If that doesn't work for you, we can do early the following week.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: pass-through-evidence-checklist.xlsx; redlines_msa_v1.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca@cloudbridge.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-01T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Partner paper redlines — pass-through and audit evidence

Rebecca — thanks, and apologies for the delay. See consolidated thoughts and a proposed clean clause attached (redlines_msa_v3.docx). Quick summary below — please consider these as Redwood's starting positions: 

1) Definition of "Pass-through Charges": limited to non‑recoverable marketplace/platform fees actually assessed by the reseller marketplace and exclusive of taxes, service markups, or internal CloudBridge fees. The draft includes an exhibit table example for the Order Form waterfall.

2) Evidence & Audit: Redwood will accept the following as sufficient evidence for reconciliation and invoicing disputes: (a) invoices from the marketplace showing fee lines, (b) payment receipts or settlement reports from the marketplace to CloudBridge, (c) a certified attestation from marketplace finance verifying the amounts.

3) Audit scope limitation: audits triggered by material billing disputes (threshold: > $25k over a rolling 12-month period). Audits will be limited to billing documents and reconciliation reports; no direct access to production logs or K/V caches. If the marketplace refuses to provide attestations, the parties will first attempt remediation via a 30-day cure period; failing that, the fallback is an indemnity limited to documented overcharges (no general access to our infra).

4) Attachments & flow: We recommend a small waterfall table in the Order Form that maps invoice party -> charge category -> marketplace fee reference. That keeps the MSA agnostic and lets each Order Form be explicit for the resale scenario.

We have redlined the MSA accordingly (see redlines_msa_v3.docx). Ben — the escrow/indemnity fallback language is included, but note procurement may push back if CloudBridge wants guaranteed recoverability. If CloudBridge can get a marketplace attestation, that will smooth it.

Next steps I propose:
- Rebecca/CloudBridge: confirm which marketplace fee categories you expect to pass through (reply on the checklist).
- If confirmed, Redwood will issue a clean MSA + Order Form exhibit in 2 business days.
- If you need broader audit rights, please identify the exact scope and we can escalate internally.
